title: The 1994 Israel-Jordan treaty says the parties will refrain from the threat or use of force
summary: The 1994 Israel-Jordan peace treaty renounces the threat or use of force between them.
body: Article 2 of the 1994 peace treaty says Israel and Jordan will refrain from the threat or use of force against each other and will settle disputes by peaceful means. The treaty is a bilateral peace. It does not settle the Palestinian question. The wording on the page includes: "neighbourly relations of co-operation between them to ensure lasting security, will refrain from the threat or use of force against each other and will settle all disputes between them by peaceful means; 4. They respect and recognise the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of every state in the region; 5. They respect and recognise the pivotal role of human development".

sources.title: Treaty of Peace between Israel and Jordan, 26 October 1994
sources.author: Avalon Project, Yale Law School
